newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Seven says no Optus settlement seen.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Seven says no Optus settlement seen.

text.p: Seven Network Ltd managing director Gary Rice said on Wednesday it was unlikely there would be any settlement between Seven and Optus Vision, before the ligitation between the two are heard in court on February 24.
"It is always difficult to say. At the moment you would have to say it appears not, but we never close off any options," Rice told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Seven is taking the court action as it claims the other Optus Vision shareholders breached the Optus Vision shareholders' agreement.

Other Optus Vission shareholders involved in the battle with Seven are Optus Communications Pty Ltd and U.S. West unit Continental CableVision, each of which own 46.5 percent, and Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd, which has a five percent stake in the pay TV group.

Seven, which has a two percent stake in Optus Vision, has said if it is successful in the litigation it would be allowed to acquire Optus Communications' stake in Optus Vision at a price which is equal to 85 percent of costs and the average of valuations in the agreement.

On Monday, Seven said it had two offers to buy the rest of Optus Vision, one of the offers was for A$648.74 million and the other was for A$533.80 million. It said it had 10 days to consider and respond to the offers.
Seven is about 23 percent-owned by its chairman Kerry Stokes and 15 percent by News Corp Ltd, which in turn jointly owns the rival Foxtel pay TV network.
At 2.20 p.m. (0320 GMT), Seven shares were one cent lower at A$4.12.
